title: Why Contract Vehicle RFQs Don't Appear on SAM.gov
summary: Task orders on SEWP, ITES, and GSA Schedules post in vehicle portals, not SAM.gov. Here's why.
body_markdown:
**Quick answer:** Most RFQs issued under federal contract vehicles never appear on SAM.gov. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) generally doesn't require agencies to publicize orders under IDIQ contracts or GSA Schedules, so those RFQs go out through each vehicle's own ordering portal, where only contract holders can see them. If your pipeline is built on SAM.gov alone, you're missing the part of the market where many resellers and their OEM partners do most of their federal business.


‍


## What is a contract vehicle RFQ?


A[contract vehicle](https://www.govly.com/blog/what-is-a-contract-vehicle) is a pre-competed contract, such as a GWAC, a multiple-award IDIQ, or a GSA Schedule, that agencies use to buy without running a brand-new open-market competition every time. The big competition happens once, when the vehicle is awarded. After that, when an agency needs something, it sends a Request for Quote (RFQ) to the companies that hold the vehicle, compares their quotes, and places a task order or delivery order with the winner.


The FAR calls this competition among holders "fair opportunity." It's real competition, but it happens inside a closed pool of contract holders, not in public. (For a refresher on how RFQs differ from RFIs and RFPs, see our[RFI vs. RFQ vs. RFP breakdown](https://www.govly.com/blog/rfi-vs-rfq-vs-rfp-whats-the-difference) .)


‍


## Why don't vehicle RFQs appear on SAM.gov?


Because the rules don't require it, and in most cases agencies have no reason to post them there.


- **Orders under IDIQ contracts:**[FAR 16.505](https://www.acquisition.gov/far/16.505) states that, in general, contracting officers do not synopsize orders under indefinite-delivery contracts. The exceptions are narrow.
- **Orders under GSA Schedules:** FAR subpart 8.4 names GSA eBuy as the electronic RFQ system for Schedule orders. For larger services orders,[FAR 8.405-2](https://www.acquisition.gov/far/8.405-2) lets the buyer either post the RFQ on eBuy or send it to as many Schedule contractors as practicable.
- **Awards, too:** Under[FAR 5.301](https://www.acquisition.gov/far/subpart-5.3) , these orders are also generally exempt from award notices on SAM.gov. They're still reported to the Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS) after award, but the RFQ itself and the competing quotes stay inside the vehicle.


The result: SAM.gov shows the solicitation for the vehicle itself, plus a handful of exception cases. The day-to-day ordering happens somewhere else.


‍


## Where do vehicle RFQs actually get posted?


Each vehicle runs its own ordering system. A few of the big ones:


- **GSA Multiple Award Schedule:** GSA eBuy.
- **NASA SEWP:** The SEWP Quote Request Tool (QRT), which sends RFQs, RFIs, and market research requests to the holders in a selected group.
- **Army ITES (ITES-4H, ITES-3S, ITES-SW2):** The CHESS IT e-mart. CHESS is the Army's mandatory source for commercial IT purchases, with limited exceptions, and its RFQs typically require quotes to be submitted through the portal.
- **NITAAC CIO-SP3, CIO-SP4, and CIO-CS:** e-GOS, NITAAC's electronic ordering system for issuing, competing, and awarding task orders.
- **Other GWACs and agency IDIQs:** Many run their own portals or route RFQs directly to holders by email.


Each one has its own login, its own notification settings, and usually shows only the requests sent to your contract group or category.


‍


## Why this matters for resellers, OEMs, and their partners


**This is where the volume is.** For a reseller on SEWP or ITES, vehicle RFQs aren't a side channel. They're the daily business.


**Response windows are short.** Vehicle RFQs often give holders days, not weeks. One Army CHESS software RFQ posted on June 10, 2026 closed on June 15. If the notice sits in one person's inbox while they're out, the quote doesn't happen.


**Coverage is fragmented by design.** A company that holds three or four vehicles is checking three or four portals, each with its own rules. Add SAM.gov and agency-specific sites, and someone is spending hours a week just looking.


**OEMs depend on partners for visibility.** Manufacturers often sell through vehicle holders rather than holding every vehicle themselves, so they only see the demand their partners pass along.


**SAM.gov notices undercount demand.** Any pipeline or market analysis built only on SAM.gov notices misses a large share of what agencies actually buy through vehicles.


‍


## How to build a process for tracking vehicle RFQs


1. **Inventory your vehicles.** List every vehicle your company and your key partners hold, the category or group you're in, and who owns each portal login.
2. **Route notifications to a team, not a person.** Make sure portal alerts are on and land in a shared inbox or channel, so nothing stalls when someone is out.
3. **Filter to what you can fill.** Scope by category, catalog, agency, and product line so the team spends its time on RFQs it can actually win.
4. **Put vehicle RFQs and SAM.gov in one pipeline.** Bid/no-bid decisions are better when every opportunity is compared in the same place.
5. **Record your own outcomes.** Award data reaches FPDS after the fact and doesn't show who else quoted, so log your wins and losses to learn which agencies and vehicles convert.
6. **Look upstream, too.** RFQs are the last step. RFIs, sources sought notices, and market research requests often come first. See[how to win federal deals before the RFQ drops](https://www.govly.com/blog/how-to-win-federal-deals-before-the-rfq-drops) .

## FAQ: contract vehicle RFQs


- **Are task order RFQs posted on SAM.gov?** Generally, no. Orders under IDIQ contracts and GSA Schedules are usually competed through the vehicle's own ordering portal rather than posted publicly.
- **Can I see vehicle RFQs if I'm not a contract holder?** Generally, no. Ordering portals limit RFQs to the holders of that vehicle, and sometimes to a specific group or category. Companies without a seat usually reach this work by teaming with or selling through a holder.
- **Do task order awards show up anywhere public?** Usually in FPDS and USAspending after award, not as SAM.gov notices. Those records show the winner and the value, but not the RFQ or the other quotes.
- **How long do holders get to respond to a vehicle RFQ?** It varies by vehicle and buyer, but windows of a few days are common. That's why alerts should go to a team rather than one person.
